prompt:
Perform one evidence-grounded COBOL compliance classification for each opaque
case using only its supplied rag_dense context. Tools and file access are not
available. Return exactly one response per alias under the required JSON
schema. A finding must use the alias as prediction.instance_id, copy the
schema. For a finding, set clause_index to the zero-based index of the supporting clause in context.retrieved_clauses. The host validates that selection and attaches that exact detector-visible clause.
The host also attaches the case identity; author the remaining prediction
fields, cite concrete source loci from the context, and include verifier hooks.
The separate claim is the citation hypothesis: write only a regulatory
obligation entailed by the selected visible clause, without COBOL identifiers
or implementation facts. Put the code-versus-clause comparison in
prediction.rationale and final_answer. In a locus, program names the containing
executable program and file names the physical copybook/source filename, never
an absolute task path. Set target_path to null unless a D1 or D5 finding
targets a composite current_value; in that case it must name a non-composite
leaf from the selected visible clause. D7 requires positive source evidence of
conformance and is never a default verdict. Abstain when evidence is
insufficient. Do not use or infer hidden labels, generation provenance,
mutation metadata, git history, file timestamps, formatting, comment
freshness, or identifier style.

ExecProbe.description:
A Tier-1 execution probe: feed ``stdin`` to the compiled locus program and
require ``expect_substring`` in stdout for the claim to hold.
ExecProbe.title: ExecProbe

StaticClaim.description:
A Tier-2 static assertion about the locus, checked against tool facts.

Any subset may be given; the attempt verifies iff *all* provided sub-claims
hold. ``dead_paragraph`` routes to call-graph reachability (D6).
StaticClaim.title: StaticClaim

SubmittedCodeLocus.description:
Provider-authored locus before host-side semantic validation.

JSON-schema structured output cannot express the cross-field rule that
multi-program loci require ``is_interprocedural=True``. Keep the submitted
value intact here, then let ``DriftPrediction`` validate it during trusted
input binding. A violation therefore abstains only that hunt instead of
invalidating every row in the provider batch.
SubmittedCodeLocus.title: SubmittedCodeLocus

SubmittedPrediction.description: Provider-authored prediction fields; trusted inputs are host-attached.
SubmittedPrediction.title: SubmittedPrediction

SubmittedResponse.description: Provider-facing final answer without provider-owned telemetry.
SubmittedResponse.title: SubmittedResponse
